title.narrative: Activity under preparation Promoting an Inclusive Green Transition in Nicaragua¿s Coffee and Cocoa value chains through Sustainable Soil Management, Traceability and Renewable Energy.

description.narrative: Coffee and cocoa are the dominant export products from Nicaragua to the European market, collectively accounting for around 50% of the EU's total imports from the country. The EU is a key market in terms of quality and prices: by 2024 EU prices for cocoa were much higher than those in the Central American market. Both coffee and cocoa are produced mainly by small farmers and cooperatives who are highly vulnerable to climate shocks, price fluctuations, and economic volatility. Women often manage post-harvest, processing and marketing activities along these two value chains. However, they face structural barriers accessing resources and technology and rarely have a decision-making role. The proposed action will strengthen the environmental sustainability and inclusiveness of Nicaragua¿s coffee and cocoa sectors, supporting their transition towards a green and resilient economy in line with EU market requirements for sustainable and deforestation-free production. It proposes supporting Nicaragua¿s transition to a green and inclusive economy through the following three components: (i) strengthen digitalisation and traceability systems in line with the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR) to enhance transparency and export competitiveness, (ii) promote sustainable soil management and circular use of agricultural residues to produce bio-inputs and alternative fertilisers, and (iii) expanding access to renewable energy through off-grid solar systems and efficient cooking technologies, directly improving women¿s livelihoods, health, and economic opportunities in production regions. The action will strengthen green skills, foster climate adaptation, and support a long-term gender-transformative shift that challenges structural barriers to women¿s access to finance and technology, where women and men benefit equally from a more sustainable, just and resilient agri-food economy.The proposed Action contributes to Priority Area 2 of the MIP 2021¿2027, Inclusive and Sustainable Economic Growth, by promoting climate-sensitive and inclusive value chains with strong potential for economic recovery, social inclusion, and women¿s participation. By addressing gender-based barriers in access to productive assets and decision-making, it will contribute to systemic change within agricultural cooperatives and small enterprises. It also supports Priority Area 1, Environment and Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation. In particular the objective of increasing environmental and biodiversity protection for sustainable ecological development and the expected result on developing alternative renewable energy sources. The intervention is fully aligned with the Gender Action Plan III (2021¿2025), particularly priorities 3.3, 3.4, and 3.6, addressing women¿s economic and social empowerment, equal participation and leadership, and opportunities within the green and digital transitions. This action contributes to SDG 5 Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls, and SDG2 (Zero Hunger), SGD 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action).
